identity.name: Lactic acid esters of mono- and diglycerides
synonyms: Lactic and fatty acid esters of glycerol
identity.chemical_class: Esterified mono- and diglycerides (lactic acid/fatty acid esters of glycerol); food emulsifier

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic ester mixture that lowers oil-water interfacial tension and stabilizes fat/water dispersions.
common_food_categories: Foods where standards of identity permit emulsifiers (broad CFR allowance)

adi.basis: EFSA 2020 concluded no need for a numerical ADI for E472a,b,c,e,f and no safety concern for E472b at reported uses/use levels.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation found no concern for genotoxicity and no safety concern for E472b at reported uses and use levels.

fda.notes: Permitted direct food additive; produced by esterification of glycerides with lactic acid and used under GMP at levels not exceeding technical effect requirements.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI: NOT LIMITED (no numerical mg/kg bw/day value specified).

concerns.summary: A mouse cream-formulation study including lactic acid esters of mono-/diglycerides reported intestinal mucus/ER-stress gene modulation, though without overt metabolic/liver toxicity over 4 weeks.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2020 concluded no safety concern for E472b at reported use levels and no need for a numerical ADI.
EFSA reported no concern for genotoxicity in the E472a-f re-evaluation.
JECFA lists ADI as NOT LIMITED (evaluation year shown as 1973).
No IARC classification listing was identified for this additive in the checked IARC classification page.

populations: Toddlers and other high per-kg consumers
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported highest E472b exposure estimates in toddlers (including high-percentile estimates), but no numerical ADI was considered necessary for E472b; classical ADI exceedance determination is therefore not directly applicable.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current regulatory evaluations (EFSA/JECFA/FDA framework) are reassuring and do not indicate major safety signals at permitted uses, while direct modern human E472b-specific evidence remains limited and some mechanistic uncertainty persists.
key_factors: EFSA 2020: no numerical ADI needed for E472b and no safety concern at reported uses
FDA permits use under 21 CFR 172.852 with GMP and manufacturing conditions
JECFA ADI listed as NOT LIMITED (1973 record)
Sparse direct human E472b epidemiological evidence
